methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - richmond.com
signals.signal_reading: Commentary identifying small-business adoption as Virginia's core AI challenge signals the shallow/concentrated risk: while NoVA attracts data center infrastructure investment, the distributed economic base lacks practical AI capability, leaving most Virginia businesses as non-participants in the AI economy.

signals.title: Christiansburg ups requirements for any future data center
signals.signal_reading: Christiansburg imposing stricter data center requirements reflects infrastructure concentration in specific nodes rather than distributed capability—physical presence of data centers doesn't equal local AI fluency, reinforcing the metro-hub pattern even as it spreads to secondary cities.

signals.title: Virginia authorizes funding for VCU to purchase Altria Center for Research and Technology - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's $250M+ Altria Center acquisition for research and technology signals Richmond's intentional build-out as a secondary AI/tech hub, potentially creating a second concentration center but not yet indicating distributed capability across Virginia's rural regions.

signals.title: Why this Virginia Tech professor says don't use AI for medical advice - roanoke.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech professor publicly educating citizens on AI limitations for medical advice represents institutional knowledge distribution beyond elite tech hubs—critical literacy building that could enable deeper, more distributed understanding rather than passive platform adoption.

signals.title: Learning Law in the AI Age - University of Virginia School of Law
signals.source: University of Virginia School of Law
signals.signal_reading: UVA Law School integrating AI into legal curriculum demonstrates professional program adaptation in established institutions, but concentrated in elite educational settings rather than community colleges or workforce programs that would signal broader distribution.
